newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Bull spread in RJR Nabisco.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Bull spread in RJR Nabisco.

text.p: A large bull spread in RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp options highlighted individual equity options trading Monday.
On the American Stock Exchange (AMEX), 14,850 contracts of the September 35 and September 40 call traded by 1315 CDT/1815 GMT. The underlying stock was unchanged at 28-7/8.
The September 35 call traded up 1/16 at 1-3/16 and the September 40 call slipped 1/8 to 5/16.
Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co in New York, said the investor bought the September 35s and sold the September 40s.

"The only thing it could be is a bull spread," said Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co. The September 35 call had open interest of 1,584 contracts and the September 40 had open interest of 2,474.
Traders said activity overall was subdued, with investors largely on the sidelines ahead of a string of U.S. economic reports due out this week, capped off Friday by the April jobless report.
"There's not a whole lot going on," one broker in Chicago said. "I don't know if anything is going to happen this week."
Several options on shares of Boeing Co were busy as the stock slid sharply after the company reported first quarter earnings that were below market expectations.
Traders also cited a report of a possible merger of Boeing competitors Lockheed Martin Corp and Airbus Industrie .
Airbus denied the British newspaper report about merger talks with Lockheed and a source familiar with Lockheed also dismissed the merger report.
Boeing was down 6-3/8 at 95-5/8 in afternoon trading after falling to 94-3/8. Turnover topped six million shares.
Among the options, the May 100 call was most active, with turnover of about 2,100 contracts. The June 95 and 100 calls traded 1,050 and 1,275 contracts, respectively.
The Boeing May 95 put was the most active put with volume of nearly 900 contracts. The put, with open interest of 1,544 contracts, rose 1-9/16 to 2-1/8.
The most active Boeing call fell 3-1/4 to 1-1/4. It had open interest of about 3,400 contracts.

Todd Salamone, senior analyst at Investment Research Institute in Cincinnati, said in a report that some investors last Friday were buying the Boeing May 105 calls expecting a positive earnings surprise.
By Monday afternoon, the May 105 call was down 1-9/16 at 7/16. Open interest in the contract, boosted by an addition of 787 on Friday, was 5,346. About 790 contracts traded Monday.
